gloss: practice makes perfect; experience teaches better than lessons

definitions.explanation: A proverb: you learn a skill better by doing it and getting used to it than by being taught. {慣|な}れよ is the old imperative of {慣|な}れる (get used to it).

examples.japanese: ⟦{運転|うんてん}→運転：01335_unten⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{習|なら}うより{慣|な}れよで、⟦とにかく→とにかく：03464_tonikaku⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ことだ。
examples.english: With driving, practice makes perfect: just get behind the wheel every day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{外国語|がいこくご}→外国語：03023_gaikokugo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{習|なら}うより{慣|な}れよ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{間違|まちが}い→間違い：03733_machigai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{恐|おそ}れ→恐れる：02023_osoreru⟧ず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦どんどん→どんどん：01261_dondon⟧⟦{話|はな}して→話す：00467_hanasu⟧みよう。
examples.english: They say practice makes perfect with foreign languages too, so let's not be afraid of mistakes and just keep talking.

notes:
USAGE:
Often followed by だ or で, or quoted with ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧. It encourages someone to start doing something instead of only studying it.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{継続|けいぞく}は{力|ちから}なり→継続は力なり：20457_keizokuhachikaranari⟧: perseverance is power — keeping at something builds ability
- ⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧: to learn, to take lessons — the first half of the proverb
